extensions.themeNote: Every semantic token is authored in both themes. The DESIGN.md frontmatter carries the light (:root) value; each colorMeta entry below carries its dark counterpart in `dark`. Neither theme is derived from the other.

display.purpose: Exactly one use: the score percentage. The largest thing in the product, because it is the only number the candidate came for.

headline.purpose: The lobby card's exam title. One per screen.

title.purpose: Pass/fail verdict (tracked to 0.12em), the desktop-required heading, dialog and drawer headings.

body.purpose: Everything else. 15px rather than 16px because the question panel is 360px wide and shares the screen with a terminal.

label.purpose: Uppercase, tracked, muted: lobby section headings, stat labels, table column heads, the code-block language tag.

data.purpose: JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals: the countdown, stat values, question ids and points, phase elapsed times, live command output.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: The faintest lift. Score banner only. Dark: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4), 0 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.3).

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Standard card lift: lobby card, desktop-required card, toasts. Dark: 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.45), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.35).

shadows.name: shadow-3
shadows.purpose: Modal depth: confirm dialog, control dialog, About drawer, and the question panel once it becomes an overlay under 900px. Dark: 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.55).

motion.name: dur-modal-out
motion.purpose: Dialog exit. Exits are shorter than entrances.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing. Decelerates without overshoot; a spring or bounce reads as unserious on an instrument.

motion.name: stagger-row
motion.purpose: Checklist row stagger, capped at 240ms, first mount only.

breakpoints.name: panel-overlay
breakpoints.purpose: Question panel leaves the flow and becomes an overlay drawer over a 36px rail.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Dialogs go full-bleed at radius 0; lobby actions stack; score rows wrap.

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: Icon controls grow to a 44px minimum. Keyed to pointer type, not width.

breakpoints.name: reflow-floor
breakpoints.purpose: The desktop-required gate must stay usable here — WCAG 1.4.10 counts 320px as a 1280px window at 400% zoom.

layering.name: z-panel
layering.purpose: Floating controls, question-panel overlay, focused skip link.

layering.name: z-overlay
layering.purpose: The control overlay sits ABOVE dialogs and drawers: it blocks a destructive rebuild and must survive every screen transition underneath it.

layering.name: z-toast
layering.purpose: Toasts stay above the overlay so a confirmation is never rendered invisible.

mirrors: images/desktop/assets/terminalrc plus its xfconf twin — the exam terminal palette

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single committed action on a screen — Start Exam, New Attempt, Retry, Got It. Exactly one per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn { background: var(--surface-raised); border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--text); padding: 0.5em 1.1em; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); cursor: pointer; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: var(--text-m, 0.9375rem); font-weight: 600; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease, transform 0.05s ease; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-contrast); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-strong); border-color: var(--accent-strong); color: var(--accent-contrast); }

components.name: Default Button
components.description: The neutral action. Rests as cool mist on a hairline; on hover the border AND text go accent while the fill stays put — it brightens rather than filling in.
components.css: .ds-btn-default { background: var(--surface-raised); border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--text); padding: 0.5em 1.1em; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); cursor: pointer; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: var(--text-m, 0.9375rem); font-weight: 600; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease, transform 0.05s ease; } .ds-btn-default:hover { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); } .ds-btn-default:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-default:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-default:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: End Exam. The only control in the system that fills on hover — deliberate, because the action is irreversible and should feel like it commits.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: var(--surface-raised); border: 1px solid var(--danger); color: var(--danger); padding: 0.5em 1.1em; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); cursor: pointer; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: var(--text-m, 0.9375rem); font-weight: 600; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease, transform 0.05s ease; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: var(--danger); color: var(--surface); } .ds-btn-danger:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Countdown Timer
components.description: Mono, bold, tabular so digits never jitter across two hours. Goes danger and pulses under five minutes — the one place intensity is permitted, because there it is information.
components.css: .ds-timer { display: inline-block; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-l, 1.125rem); font-weight: 700; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: 0.03em; padding: 0.2em 0.6em; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); background: var(--surface-raised); border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--accent); } .ds-timer-low { color: var(--danger); border-color: var(--danger); animation: ds-timer-pulse 1.5s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-timer-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.55; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-timer-low { animation: none; } }

components.name: Instance Chip
components.description: Which box to ssh into — the single most load-bearing fact per question, and the only pill carrying a full accent treatment.
components.css: .ds-instance-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4em; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-s, 0.85rem); color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); border: 1px solid var(--accent); border-radius: var(--radius-pill, 999px); padding: 0.15em 0.75em; }

components.name: Bank Card (active)
components.description: An exam in the lobby catalog. Rests on the page fill with a hairline; hover takes the border to accent; the active exam takes an accent border and blue wash. Its badge switches to accent-strong, because plain accent falls to 4.0:1 on that wash.
components.css: .ds-bank-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.25rem; width: 100%; text-align: left; background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); padding: 0.75rem 1rem; cursor: pointer; font-family: var(--font-sans); color: var(--text); transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-bank-card:hover { border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-bank-card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-bank-card-active { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); } .ds-bank-title { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; flex-wrap: wrap; font-weight: 700; } .ds-bank-badge { font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--accent-strong); border: 1px solid var(--accent-strong); border-radius: var(--radius-pill, 999px); padding: 0.05em 0.6em; } .ds-bank-meta { color: var(--text-muted); font-size: var(--text-s, 0.85rem); }

components.name: Click-to-Copy Value
components.description: Signature component. Every inline value in a question is a button that reads as part of the sentence — it borrows the inline-code look and reveals its affordance only on hover or focus. The mono font is the only resting signal, which under the Mono-For-Truth Rule already means 'this is a literal value'.
components.html: Create a Deployment named in namespace .
components.css: .ds-copy-host { font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: var(--text-m, 0.9375rem); line-height: 1.55; color: var(--text); margin: 0; } .ds-copy-value { display: inline; padding: 0; border: 0; background: none; font: inherit; color: inherit; cursor: pointer; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); } .ds-copy-value code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.92em; background: var(--bg); padding: 0.1em 0.3em; border-radius: 3px; border: 1px solid transparent; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-copy-value:hover code, .ds-copy-value:focus-visible code { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent-strong); } .ds-copy-icon { font-size: 0.75em; margin-left: 0.25em; color: var(--text-muted); opacity: 0; } .ds-copy-value:hover .ds-copy-icon, .ds-copy-value:focus-visible .ds-copy-icon { opacity: 1; } .ds-copy-value:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Toast
components.description: Time warnings and connection state. A 3px left border carries the severity; warning swaps it to amber. Sits above the control overlay so a confirmation is never rendered invisible.
components.html: 5 minutes remaining.
components.css: .ds-toast { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 380px; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-left: 3px solid var(--accent); border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.1), 0 2px 4px rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.08); padding: 0.75rem 0.75rem 0.75rem 1rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: var(--text-m, 0.9375rem); color: var(--text); } .ds-toast-warning { border-left-color: var(--warn); } .ds-toast-message { flex: 1; } .ds-toast-dismiss { background: transparent; border: none; color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; padding: 0 0.2em; } .ds-toast-dismiss:hover { color: var(--text); } .ds-toast-dismiss:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: A fenced block reads as ONE object: the figure owns the border, the radius and the body background, with a language tag and a copy-whole-block control in its head. Keyword highlighting uses accent-strong, because plain accent measures only 4.1:1 on this fill in the light theme.
components.css: .ds-code-block { margin: 0.75rem 0; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); background: var(--surface-raised); overflow: hidden; } .ds-code-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--surface); } .ds-code-lang { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.75rem); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--text-muted); } .ds-code-copy { background: none; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-s, 6px); color: var(--accent); cursor: pointer; padding: 0.25rem 0.5rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.75rem); } .ds-code-copy:hover { border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-code-copy:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-code-block pre { margin: 0; padding: 0.75rem; overflow-x: auto; background: transparent; border: none; } .ds-code-block code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.92em; color: var(--text); } .ds-kw { color: var(--accent-strong); } .ds-cm { color: var(--text-muted); font-style: italic; }

components.name: Rebuild Phase Row
components.description: Signature component. A cluster rebuild takes minutes, so the checklist is built to be watched: mark | label | elapsed, with the running phase's live command output spanning underneath, clipped to one line so a long line cannot reflow the dialog on every poll. The running phase gets a rotating arc — without visible motion a four-minute wait reads as frozen.

components.css: .ds-phases { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: var(--text-m, 0.9375rem); } .ds-phase { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1em 1fr auto; gap: 0.25rem 0.75rem; align-items: baseline; color: var(--text-muted); } .ds-phase-done { color: var(--text); } .ds-phase-running { color: var(--accent); } .ds-phase-failed { color: var(--danger); } .ds-phase-mark { font-family: var(--font-mono); width: 1em; text-align: center; } .ds-phase-elapsed { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-s, 0.85rem); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--text-muted); } .ds-phase-detail { grid-column: 2 / -1; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.75rem); color: var(--text-muted); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-phase-spinner { width: 0.75em; height: 0.75em; margin: 0 0.125em; align-self: center; border: 2px solid currentColor; border-right-color: transparent; border-radius: 50%; animation: ds-phase-spin 0.8s linear infinite; } @keyframes ds-phase-spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-phase-spinner { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
This is the interface a person looks at while a clock they cannot pause counts down toward a result that matters to them. Everything in the system follows from that one fact. It is an instrument panel, not a product tour: it reports state accurately, it never competes for attention, and it never performs. The phrasing is the codebase's own — "a spring or a bounce reads as unserious" — and it generalises past motion into every other decision here.

The philosophy is restraint as respect. A candidate under time pressure has no attention to spare, so the interface spends none of it. Surfaces are quiet: three cool-slate tones separated by hairline borders, with the accent held back until the user reaches for something. Type does the structural work that colour and ornament would do in a louder system. Motion is short, decelerating, and never overshoots. The result should feel less like an app and more like well-made equipment — the kind you stop noticing once you are working.

The one place the system permits intensity is where intensity is information: the countdown turning red and pulsing under five minutes, a failed phase in the rebuild checklist, a pass/fail verdict. Those are readings, not decoration. Everything else recedes.
keyCharacteristics: Kubernetes blue used referentially on cool slate, in two fully specified themes — every semantic token has a light and a dark value, and components never hardcode a colour.
Contrast is a ledger, not an intention: every text pairing carries its measured ratio in a comment beside the token.
Monospace is a semantic choice — it marks anything the candidate must type, match, or trust as a measurement.
Tone and hairline borders carry depth; shadow is reserved for things genuinely floating above the page.
Motion is written additively inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so the calm state is the default rather than the fallback.
No text inputs exist anywhere in the product. Real input happens in the terminal.

rules.name: The Contrast Ledger Rule
rules.body: Every text-on-background pairing carries its measured ratio in a comment beside the token in tokens.css. A pairing that lands under 4.5:1 gets a substitute token, never a waiver — which is why accent-strong exists at all. axe runs in the test suite but jsdom has no layout engine, so the colour-contrast rule is skipped there: the ledger IS the check, and it is re-verified by hand whenever a value moves.

rules.name: The Rare Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is earned, not applied. At rest, a screen is slate and ink; blue arrives on hover, focus, selection, live progress, and exactly one filled button. If a new screen reads as blue before the user touches it, the accent has been used as decoration.

rules.name: The Three Mirrors Rule
rules.body: These values live in three places outside tokens.css — the Go locked page, the favicon, and the exam terminal's palette plus its xfconf twin. A colour change is never a one-file change. The candidate sees the same palette in the browser chrome and inside the terminal they are working in.

rules.name: The No Marks Rule
rules.body: The blue is referential; the marks are not borrowed. No Kubernetes or CNCF logo, wordmark, or mark appears anywhere in the product, and the non-affiliation notice stays in the lobby footer and the About panel.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Truth Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono marks anything the candidate must type, match, or trust as a measurement: resource names, ids, points, durations, paths, command output, the score. IBM Plex Sans is for prose that explains. The test is mechanical — if a value could be pasted into a terminal, or compared digit by digit, it is mono. This is why every click-to-copy value in a question is mono: the font is the affordance.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything that ticks uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums — the countdown, the control-job elapsed clock, per-phase timings. A digit that changes width makes a stable reading look unstable, and the countdown is on screen for two hours.

rules.name: The Unbroken Height Rule
rules.body: html, body, #root and main all assert height: 100%. A percentage height resolves to auto the moment one ancestor in the chain is content-sized, and every full-height screen depends on that chain being intact. Do not add a wrapper element to the chain without giving it a height.

rules.name: The Scroll-Inside Rule
rules.body: Wide or long content scrolls inside its own container, never the page: tables get overflow-x: auto with overscroll-behavior-x: contain, code blocks scroll horizontally within the block, and in the control dialog only the checklist scrolls while the header and actions stay pinned — the progress a user is waiting on must never scroll out of view.

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: If an element is anchored to the page, it gets tone and a hairline border. If it floats above the page — a card, a dialog, a drawer, a toast — it gets exactly one of the three shadows. There is no hover-lift, no raised button, no resting elevation on anything in normal flow.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every surface declares its edge with a 1px border. This system has no borderless floating cards; the border does the work that a heavier shadow would do elsewhere, which is what keeps the flat state readable in both themes.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: Anchored gets 6px, floating gets 10px, status gets pill, and a new component picks from those three rather than introducing its own. Exactly two exceptions are documented, and a third should not be added: inline code uses 3px, because a box sized to a few characters needs a corner proportional to itself rather than to a button; and below 600px full-bleed dialogs drop to radius 0 — a sheet that reaches every edge should not pretend to have corners.

rules.name: The Motion-Additive Rule
rules.body: Motion is written inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), never as a default that a reduce-guard later neutralises. base.css carries the global guard as well, but authoring additively means a reduced-motion user never depends on an animation being correctly cancelled and never downloads a frame of it. Layout must be identical either way: .screen carries its height: 100% outside the media query for exactly this reason, and every keyframe plays forward to the element's real style, so a screen that never runs its animation still ends up visible.

dos: Do define both theme values for every new semantic token, in tokens.css, and record the measured contrast ratio beside it. A token that exists in one theme is a bug in the other.
Do use accent-strong for accent-coloured text on accent-soft or surface-raised. Plain accent measures 4.0:1 and 4.1:1 there — under the floor.
Do reach for tone and a 1px hairline border first. Add a shadow only when the element genuinely floats above the page.
Do set anything the candidate must type, match, or read as a measurement in JetBrains Mono, and add tabular-nums if it changes over time.
Do pick radii from the three that exist: 6px anchored, 10px floating, pill for status.
Do write new motion additively inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, animating only transform and opacity.
Do keep every user-facing string in ui/src/strings.ts.
Do change all three mirrors when a colour changes — the Go locked page, the favicon, and the terminal palette with its xfconf twin.
Do make wide content scroll inside its own container, and keep pinned what the user is waiting on.
donts: Don't hardcode a colour in a component. Every value comes from a semantic token, without exception.
Don't use the accent as a resting surface. If a screen reads as blue before the user touches anything, the accent has become decoration.

Don't add springs, bounces, overshoot, gradient fills, emoji, or a celebratory flourish on a pass. The product reports a result; it does not congratulate. A spring reads as unserious on an instrument.
Don't build overlay tutorials, spotlight tours, or coach marks measured against live layout. Explain a screen with a self-contained drawing that holds its own proportions.
Don't let the score page or the lobby drift toward a dashboard — dense chrome, charts for their own sake, cards competing for attention. The score page is one column, and one number matters.
Don't hide an element with a transform when it must be keyboard-reachable. Use the .sr-only clip idiom; a translate is proportional to the element's own height and will eventually leak.
Don't add a wrapper to the html/body/#root/main height chain without giving it a height.
Don't let .desktop-canvas take its size from its own content. It is absolutely positioned so noVNC's ResizeObserver cannot enter a resize feedback loop; that is structural, not stylistic.
Don't introduce a text input reflexively. This product has none, and the terminal is where real input belongs.
Don't load a font, stylesheet, or icon from a CDN. Everything ships bundled — the exam must not depend on the network.
